title: Degree reduction under coordinate differentiation
statement: Let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$, let $i\in[n]$, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. If $F(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k+1$, then the coefficient family formed from the Fourier coefficients of the Boolean-cube derivative of $F$ has degree at most $k$; that is, its coefficient at $S$ vanishes whenever $|S|>k$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Define $A_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ and $D_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_{S\cup\{i\}}\prod_{j\in S}x_j$. If $F$ has degree at most $k+1$, where $k\ge0$ is an integer, then $D_i$ has degree at most $k$.
